claim_judgments.rationale: C0000 states an unconditional requirement that an employer must have an emergency action plan, omitting the critical statutory condition 'whenever an OSHA standard in this part requires one' as well as the application clause in 1910.38(a). This renders the scope impermissibly overbroad and the summary inaccurate.

C0001 captures the general rule that an emergency action plan must be in writing, kept in the workplace, and available for employee review, but fails to incorporate or reference the exception in paragraph (b) for employers with 10 or fewer employees who may communicate the plan orally. This causes the stated scope and summary to be overbroad relative to the source rule.
C0002 accurately extracts the permissive exception in 1910.38(b), allowing employers with 10 or fewer employees to communicate the plan orally to employees rather than maintaining a written plan.

C0003 accurately states the mandatory duty in 1910.38(e) for employers to designate and train employees to assist in a safe and orderly evacuation of other employees, correctly inheriting the general scope of application.

unit_judgments.rationale: C0000 omits the explicit scope condition 'whenever an OSHA standard in this part requires one' and the rule that requirements apply to each such plan, leaving the unit only partially covered.
C0001 captures the written plan requirement but omits the explicit qualification/exception for employers with 10 or fewer employees and lacks a link to C0002.
C0002 faithfully and fully captures the oral plan permission for employers with 10 or fewer employees.
No claim in the draft covers the minimum element requirement for procedures for reporting a fire or other emergency under 1910.38(c)(1).
No claim in the draft covers the minimum element requirement for emergency evacuation procedures, including evacuation type and exit route assignments under 1910.38(c)(2).
No claim in the draft covers procedures for employees who remain to operate critical plant operations under 1910.38(c)(3).
No claim in the draft covers procedures to account for all employees after evacuation under 1910.38(c)(4).
No claim in the draft covers procedures for employees performing rescue or medical duties under 1910.38(c)(5).
No claim in the draft covers the requirement to include names or job titles of contact persons for plan information under 1910.38(c)(6).
No claim in the draft covers the employer requirement to have and maintain an employee alarm system under 1910.38(d).
No claim in the draft covers the requirements for distinctive signals and compliance with § 1910.165 for employee alarm systems under 1910.38(d).
C0003 fully and faithfully retains the requirement to designate and train employees to assist in evacuation under 1910.38(e).
No claim in the draft covers the requirement to review the plan when developed or initially assigned under 1910.38(f)(1).
No claim in the draft covers the requirement to review the plan when an employee's responsibilities change under 1910.38(f)(2).
No claim in the draft covers the requirement to review the plan when the plan is changed under 1910.38(f)(3).
